data.name: Thais
data.gender_notes: Thais is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Thais was a goddess revered for her ability to grant fertility and prosperity. In the New Testament, Thais is mentioned in the story of the repentant sinner who anointed Jesus' feet with her tears and costly perfume. The name Thais carries the meaning “Goddess of Fertility” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Thais usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of fertility and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Thais belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Fertility.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Thais total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: תאייס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם תאייס מקורו בשפה היוונית ומשמעותו 'קורבן לאלוקים' או 'שייך לאל'. הוא מופיע בתנ'ך רק בספר דניאל, פרק ה', פסוקים ט' ו-י', שם הוא מתייחס לאחד משרי המלך בלשאצר. השם תאייס משמש גם כזכר וגם כנקבה, אך הוא נדיר יותר כשם פרטי לנשים.

in_greek.name: Θάϊς
in_greek.meaning: Κόρη του Θεού, θυσία εις τον Θεόν
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Θάϊς (Thais) είναι ελληνικής προέλευσης και σημαίνει 'κόρη του Θεού' ή 'θυσία εις τον Θεόν'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, δεν αναφέρεται συγκεκριμένα, αλλά το αντίστοιχο εβραϊκό όνομα מָהַתְלָאִים (Mahathlai) αναφέρεται στο βιβλίο του Νεεμίας, κεφάλαιο 12, εδάφιο 14, ως ένας από τους ιερείς που επέστρεψαν από την εξορία στη Βαβυλώνα.

in_latin.name: Thais
in_latin.meaning: Gift of God, devoted to God
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Thais is derived from the Greek name Θάϊς (Thais), which means 'gift of God' or 'devoted to God'. In the early Christian Church, the name Thais was used to signify a person dedicated to spiritual pursuits and devotion to God. The Latin usage of the name maintains its Greek origin and connotation.

in_english.name: Thais
in_english.meaning: Gift of God, devoted to God, pure
in_english.long_meaning: The name Thais originates from the Greek language, meaning 'gift of God' or 'devoted to God'. It is associated with purity and spiritual dedication. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, its Hebrew and Greek roots link it to biblical names signifying devotion to God. Historically, Thais has been used in Christian traditions to denote a person of strong faith and spiritual commitment.

data.cultural_impact: The name Thais may evoke the image of ancient Greek fertility goddesses, highlighting a connection to the rich cultural heritage of Greece.
data.spiritual_significance: However, for Christians, the name Thais holds a deeper spiritual meaning, as it is associated with the woman in the New Testament who was a sinner and showed great devotion to Jesus through her tears and costly perfume. This biblical story reminds us of the power of repentance and faith, and the importance of selfless acts of love and devotion to God.
